answer: A walnut trading cooperative enrolls agent operators at simultaneous local gatherings. When the lantern signal starts, witnesses issue one voting credential to each physically present person and keep everyone in the room until enrollment closes. A mirror identity cannot put the same body in two rooms at once; extra software accounts receive no extra credential. A farm must recruit and transport more people or bribe witnesses, adding labor and coordination costs. This assumes honest headcounts and a short shared window; credential lending and exclusion of distant users remain risks.
